decisions.executionNote: Begin a continuous elbow-up approach with the left arm toward the set square, pitching the open gripper downward. Right arm remains at origin.
Move toward the left end of the straightedge while increasing downward pitch, with small continuous increments.
Approach above the left section of the ruler, maintaining the current elbow branch and completing the downward grasp approach.
Orient the gripper across the narrow straightedge before descending; keep clear of the blocks.
The near ruler end shifted during orientation. Raise slightly and center above its new position before closing across its width.
Fine-center the open jaws on the left section of the ruler and lower cautiously to a side grasp.
Close around the ruler only, keeping its working edge on the table; verify retention visually before pushing.
Yaw the held straightedge toward a transverse row orientation without lifting any blocks; inspect that the ruler follows the jaws.
The ruler did not follow the yaw test, so reopen and lower the grasp slightly before closing again; no cube contact yet.
Test a small table-parallel translation with the gripper closed to determine whether the ruler is retained.
Advance the set square slowly and reduce its diagonal angle, watching the edge motion rather than relying on gripper state.
Slide the ruler forward toward the three blocks while bringing its long edge closer to a straight transverse orientation.
Continue leveling the ruler's long edge in front of the cubes, sliding on the tabletop and leaving the cubes ungrasped.
Bring the nearly horizontal straightedge into the backs of the cubes with a slow, level forward push.
The ruler's far end lags, so hold the left end steady and bring the right arm toward its own end for a controlled two-ended push.
Replan the rejected right-arm start with smaller pitch and translation increments, keeping the left ruler end stationary.
Approach the ruler's right end from the right workspace, pitching down while maintaining clearance and holding the left end fixed.
Continue the right arm's elbow-up approach above the outer ruler end, keeping both grippers away from the cubes.
Finish pitching the right gripper downward above the ruler, leaving room to orient the jaws across its width.
Rotate the right jaws across the ruler while centering above its right end; left grip remains stationary.
Center the right gripper slightly inside the ruler tip and continue the widthwise jaw orientation above the surface.
Lower the oriented right jaws onto the ruler's outer section for a side grasp, without approaching the blocks.
Fine-center the right jaws across the ruler and close at table height, keeping both tools clear of the cube tops.
Bring the right end forward to level the ruler edge with the left end, using a slow surface-parallel push.
Push with both ruler ends, slightly advancing the right end more to remove the remaining skew and seat all cube faces against the edge.
Advance the now-level ruler evenly so the remaining skewed cube rotates flush with the same straight edge; keep all cubes on the table.
The three cubes appear straight and parallel. Withdraw the ruler evenly along the table to separate it before releasing and resetting both arms.
Release the ruler on the table and raise the empty open grippers for a collision-free reset, leaving the aligned cubes undisturbed.
Retract both empty arms within their own workspaces and unwind wrist yaw toward the origin configuration, preserving the elbow-up branch.
Continue the empty-arm reset with smooth backward motion and yaw unwinding; the cubes remain undisturbed in a straight row.
Continue reset from the executed prefix only, reducing wrist-yaw and translation increments after the continuity interruption.
Finish unwinding yaw and return each wrist over its own starting lane, preparing to restore the initial forward-facing pitch.
Restore the forward-facing wrist orientation while gently returning both EEs toward their recorded origin poses.
Continue restoring the initial wrist pitch and EE height with small continuous increments, keeping the grippers open.
Approach the recorded reset poses while restoring wrist pitch smoothly. The aligned blocks and released ruler remain stationary.
Complete the smooth return to both recorded origin poses, leaving the three aligned cubes untouched and both grippers open.
